syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: The grandmother and the grandfather's portrait

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the author portrays his grandmother's appearance and inner beauty.
Interpret the similes and images used to describe the grandmother.

topics.title: Village days and the turning-point

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the grandmother and the author spent their days in the village.
Explain why the move to the city school changed their friendship.

topics.title: Seclusion, sparrows and departure abroad

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the grandmother accepted her loneliness after the author went to university.
Evaluate the grandmother's calm and unsentimental strength of character.

topics.title: Homecoming, death and the mourning sparrows

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the grandmother's unusual behaviour on the evening of the author's return.
Interpret the sparrows' silent mourning at the grandmother's death.

topics.title: Working with words and noticing form

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the different senses of 'tell' and 'take' as used in the text.
Identify words that describe a manner of walking.
Recognise the past perfect form used to recount the distant past.

topics.title: Poem: A Photograph (Shirley Toulson)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three phases of time depicted in the poem's three stanzas.
Interpret the poem's treatment of loss, memory and the transience of human life.

chapters.title: We're Not Afraid to Die... if We Can All Be Together

topics.title: The dream voyage and its early stages

concepts.learning_objective: Recall who undertook the voyage, why, and in what boat.
Trace the route of the first leg and explain why extra crew were taken on.

topics.title: The great wave strikes on January 2

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the precautions taken to protect the ship as the weather worsened.
Interpret the narrator's description of the giant wave and his experience of it.

topics.title: Fighting the flood and the children's courage

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the steps taken to check the flooding of the ship.
Evaluate how the children's behaviour reveals courage and selflessness.

topics.title: The search for Ile Amsterdam

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the narrator navigated without proper instruments to find the island.
Analyse how optimism and family bonds helped the voyagers endure the direst stress.

topics.title: Words and expressions from the account

concepts.learning_objective: Identify ship terms that have other common meanings and use them in context.
Infer the meaning of phrasal verbs and expressions from their context in the account.

topics.title: Tut's story and the night he left his tomb

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the key facts of Tut's life, death and the 1922 discovery of his tomb.
Interpret the imagery and beliefs (such as the pharaoh's curse) in the opening scene of the account.

topics.title: Howard Carter's investigation of the mummy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why and how Carter freed the mummy from its coffin and adornments.
Describe the treasures and everyday objects buried with Tut and what they reveal about Egyptian beliefs.

topics.title: Changing archaeology: from X-ray to CT scan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the aims and tools of archaeology have changed since Carter's time.
Explain how computed tomography works and why it was used on Tut.

topics.title: Tut's dynasty and the Amarna period

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Akhenaten's religious changes and why they were seen as strange.
Explain Tut's change of name, his restoration of the old ways and his place among Egypt's mummies.

topics.title: The night of the CT scan

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the events of the scan night and what they reveal about the people involved.
Analyse the mood and figures of speech in the closing description of the account.

topics.title: The Laburnum Top (Ted Hughes)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the images, colours and comparisons used to describe the tree and the goldfinch.
Explain the engine metaphor for the goldfinch and her family.
Analyse how the stillness at the beginning and end frames the poem.

topics.title: The Voice of the Rain (Walt Whitman)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the speakers and the meaning of key words in the poem.
Relate the poem's description of the rain to the water cycle.
Explain the parallel drawn between the rain and a song or poem.

chapters.title: The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role

topics.title: The Green Movement and the holistic view of the earth

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how and when the Green Movement began and how widely it spread.
Explain the shift from a mechanistic to a holistic, ecological view of the earth as a living organism.

topics.title: Sustainable development and the world's most dangerous animal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the 1987 definition of sustainable development and its meaning.
Interpret the Lusaka zoo notice and the shift from domination to partnership.

topics.title: The earth's principal biological systems

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four principal biological systems and their role in the global economy.
Explain how over-use is depleting fisheries, forests, grasslands and croplands.

topics.title: Forests, law and the environment in India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Article 48A and the author's criticism of weak enforcement of laws in India.
Interpret the data on the depletion of India's forests.

topics.title: Population growth and poverty

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the figures showing the rapid growth of world population.
Evaluate the author's argument linking development, family planning and poverty.

topics.title: The Era of Responsibility

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the transcending concern and the role of industry in the Era of Responsibility.
Interpret the Thatcher and Lester Brown quotations about our duty to future generations.

topics.title: The poem 'Childhood' by Markus Natten

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the themes of rationalism, hypocrisy and individuality in the poem.
Interpret the poet's feeling towards childhood and the poem's devices.

topics.title: The journey to a different Bombay

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the details of Bombay and the train journey that show Gangadharpant is in a different world.
Explain what the signs of British rule in Bombay reveal about this alternative India.

topics.title: History rewritten in the Asiatic Society library

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the point at which history changed, as found in Gangadharpant's own volumes.
Describe the consequences of the Maratha victory for India in the alternative history.

topics.title: The Bakhar and the lecture at Azad Maidan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Bakhar and the torn page serve as evidence of Gangadharpant's experience.
Interpret the conflict over the empty chair and its effect on Professor Gaitonde.

topics.title: Rajendra's scientific explanation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the catastrophe theory to the Battle of Panipat as Rajendra does.
Explain how lack of determinism in quantum theory leads to the idea of many worlds and transitions between them.

topics.title: Words and forms in the story

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the meaning of idiomatic expressions used in the story from context.
Recognise conditional sentences that express unreal and hypothetical conditions.

topics.title: Leaving Ravu and crossing the Changtang

concepts.learning_objective: Recall Lhamo's farewell gift and Tsetan's short cut towards Mount Kailash.
Describe the kyang, drokbas and Tibetan mastiffs seen on the plains and explain why mastiffs were prized.

topics.title: Crossing the high mountain pass

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Tsetan got the vehicle across the snow and ice on the pass.
Relate the author's headache and the hissing petrol tank to the effects of high altitude.
Identify how the top of the pass was marked and the custom observed there.

topics.title: The salt lake, Hor and Lake Manasarovar

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the salt-lake workcamp and the geological origin of the plateau's salt flats.
Contrast the author's bleak experience of Hor with the sanctity of Lake Manasarovar and earlier travellers' accounts.

topics.title: A troubled night and Tibetan medicine at Darchen

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the author's breathing difficulty and fear of sleeping at Darchen.
Interpret the doctor's treatment, its effect and Tsetan's parting remark.

topics.title: Waiting in Darchen and meeting Norbu

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the author was disappointed with Darchen and felt his options were limited.
Analyse why Norbu, though ill-equipped, seemed an ideal companion for the kora.

topics.title: Language, words and style of the travelogue

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Tsetan's English and the use of interpreters in the narrative.
Infer the meanings of Tibetan words and uncommon adjectives used in the text.
Recognise how active voice shapes the style of the narrative.

topics.title: Father to Son (poem)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the lines that show the distance and lack of understanding between father and son.
Interpret the father's helplessness, the prodigal-son allusion and the longing for reconciliation.
Recall the poet and describe the stanza form and rhyme pattern of the poem.

topics.title: Stanza 1: Reason questions old beliefs

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the poet wonders whether childhood ended when he ceased to be eleven.
Analyse how logical reasoning about Heaven and Hell marks the end of childhood.

topics.title: Stanza 2: The hypocrisy of adults

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the poet's discovery that adults do not practise the love they preach.

topics.title: Stanza 3: A mind of one's own

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how forming independent thoughts signals the loss of childhood.

topics.title: Final stanza and central theme

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the image of childhood hidden in an infant's face.
Identify the poem's theme of growing up and the loss of innocence.

topics.title: Poetic devices and structure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the refrain and rhetorical questions and explain their effect.
Identify rhyme and repetition in the poem and evaluate their purpose.

topics.title: Effective writing and the purpose of note-making

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the abilities a student needs to write effectively, such as coherence, cohesive devices and command of grammar.
Explain why note-making is an important study skill useful at study and at work.

topics.title: Reading for main points: underlining and questioning

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the important information in a passage by underlining it.
Frame and answer questions while reading to pick out the main points of a passage.

topics.title: Writing and organising notes

concepts.learning_objective: Write points in note form using phrases, colons and long dashes without full verb forms.
Distinguish between the letter/figure system and the decimal system of dividing notes.

topics.title: Characteristics of good notes

concepts.learning_objective: Use abbreviations and symbols and omit articles, prepositions and conjunctions in notes.
Evaluate whether a set of notes is short, logical and meaningful when read again.

topics.title: Practice: making notes on the formation of coal and petroleum

concepts.learning_objective: Convert verb-based statements into noun-headed note points.
Combine and group related points from a passage into ordered notes.

topics.title: What summarising is and how it differs from note-making

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a summary from notes in purpose, length and form.
Recall the steps of summarising and how points are expanded and linked.

topics.title: Precise expression: one word for many

concepts.learning_objective: Replace a long phrase with a single precise word, as in 'precocious' or 'versatile'.

topics.title: Reducing the soybean passage

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the guideline that a summary is usually about one-third of the original.
Identify apposition, present participles and a postponed main verb as devices that shorten a summary.

topics.title: Practice passage: Green Sahara

concepts.learning_objective: Understand the main facts and causes described in 'Green Sahara'.
Evaluate which details of a passage belong in its summary.

topics.title: The purpose of sub-titling

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why sub-titles are given to sections of a long piece of writing.
Frame a suitable sub-heading that captures the main idea of a section.

topics.title: Urban decay in Indian cities

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the 1994 Surat plague exposed urban decay and neglected public health.
Explain how cities chased 'modernisation' at the cost of basic civic reform.

topics.title: Sanitation, public health and urban transport
topics.ncert_sections: Article: sanitation data and transport paragraphs

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the Census 2001 figures on latrines and drainage in urban households.
Analyse how automobile-centred planning endangers pedestrians and cyclists.

topics.title: The Curitiba model of urban planning

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Curitiba's low-cost transport and land-use measures.
Explain how Curitiba managed floods compared with Indian cities.

topics.title: A rights-based approach to urban renewal

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the writer's call for a rights-based, inclusive model of urban renewal.

topics.title: Getting started: brainstorming and listing ideas

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how brainstorming or jotting ideas around a central topic helps a writer begin an essay.
Select relevant points from a random list and expand each into a sentence.

topics.title: Developing points into paragraphs

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that an essay usually opens with a definition or short description of the topic.
Show how related points are grouped and developed into connected paragraphs.

topics.title: Characteristics of a good essay

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish unity (all parts linked to the main subject) from coherence (logical sequence of ideas).
Apply relevance and proportion when choosing and weighting content in an essay.

topics.title: Model essay: The Importance of Games

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the physical benefits of games argued in the model essay.
Interpret the moral benefits and the dangers of games discussed in the essay.

topics.title: Passage analysis and essay structure

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the introduction-body-conclusion plan of the model essay paragraph by paragraph.
Plan an essay on a new topic by applying the steps shown in the chapter.
